name: strbuild
algorithm: Growable string building loop: build docs documents from an empty standard string builder by appending literals, slices, repeated chunks and formatted integers for lines records per document, then fold the FNV-1a 64 checksum and byte length of each built string (README.md).

skip.c: no std growable string builder in C
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; there is no checked arithmetic to remove

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares standard library string builders, each with its own growth policy; the FNV-1a 64 checksum plus byte length checks that every builder assembled the exact same bytes
notes: Each document starts from an empty builder (never pre-sized) and grows geometrically across lines structured ASCII records combining literals, dictionary slices, source-text subslices, repeated 2-byte chunks and decimal integers.
C#'s StringBuilder stores UTF-16 chunks internally; because every appended character is ASCII, reading sb.GetChunks() hashes the exact same byte sequence without an extra UTF-8 re-encoding pass.
